nodes.summary: For every capacity $c$, the empty LRU cache of capacity $c$ is the cache with no entries.
nodes.title: Empty LRU cache

nodes.summary: Given a key $k$ and a list of key–value pairs, erasing $k$ deletes every pair whose key is $k$ and keeps the other pairs in their original order. When the keys in the list are pairwise distinct, at most one pair is deleted.
nodes.title: Erasing a key from a list of entries

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be an LRU cache of capacity $c$, let $k'$ be a key not stored in $C$, and let $k$ be a key stored in $C$. If $k$ is no longer stored after putting $k'$ with any value $v$ into $C$, then $C$ held exactly $c$ entries and $k$ is the last key of $C$, that is, the least recently used one.
nodes.title: The evicted key is the least recently used one

nodes.summary: Two LRU caches with the same key type, value type and capacity are equal if their lists of entries are equal.
nodes.title: Extensionality of LRU caches

nodes.summary: If an LRU cache stores the pair $(k, v)$, then looking up $k$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: A lookup of a stored key returns its value

nodes.summary: For every LRU cache and every key $k$, the keys of the cache obtained by looking up $k$ are pairwise distinct.
nodes.title: Lookups keep keys distinct

nodes.summary: If the key $k$ is not stored in an LRU cache, then looking up $k$ returns no value and leaves the cache unchanged.
nodes.title: A lookup of an absent key misses

nodes.summary: For every LRU cache and every key $k$, the list of entries of the cache after looking up $k$ is a permutation of the list of entries before.
nodes.title: A lookup permutes the entries

nodes.summary: If an LRU cache stores the pair $(k, v)$, then after looking up $k$ the most recently used (first) entry of the cache is $(k, v)$.
nodes.title: A successful lookup moves the entry to the front

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be an LRU cache of capacity $c$ that holds fewer than $c$ entries or already stores the key $k$. Then for every key $k' \ne k$ and every value $v$, looking up $k'$ in the cache obtained by putting the binding $(k, v)$ into $C$ returns the same optional value as looking up $k'$ in $C$.
nodes.title: A put without eviction preserves lookups of other keys

nodes.summary: For every LRU cache of positive capacity, every key $k$ and every value $v$, looking up $k$ in the cache obtained by putting the binding $(k, v)$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: Lookup after insertion into an LRU cache

nodes.summary: For every LRU cache of capacity $c$ and every key $k$, the cache after looking up $k$ holds at most $c$ entries.
nodes.title: Lookup respects the capacity

nodes.summary: For every LRU cache and every key $k$, the cache after looking up $k$ holds exactly as many entries as before.
nodes.title: Lookup preserves the size

nodes.summary: Looking up a key $k$ in an LRU cache returns an optional value together with a cache. If the cache stores a binding $(k, v)$, the result is $v$ together with the cache in which that binding is moved to the front and the other entries keep their order; otherwise the result is no value together with the unchanged cache.
nodes.title: LRU cache lookup

nodes.summary: The keys stored in any LRU cache are pairwise distinct.
nodes.title: Keys of an LRU cache are distinct

nodes.summary: The key list of an LRU cache is the list of the keys of its entries in the order of the cache, so the most recently used key comes first.
nodes.title: Key list of an LRU cache

nodes.summary: For a type $K$ of keys, a type $V$ of values and a natural number $c$, an LRU cache of capacity $c$ is a list of key-value pairs in $K \times V$, ordered from most to least recently used, whose keys are pairwise distinct and whose length is at most $c$.
nodes.title: Least-recently-used cache

nodes.summary: For every LRU cache and every key $k$, a key-value pair is stored in the cache after looking up $k$ if and only if it was stored in the cache before the lookup.
nodes.title: Lookup preserves the stored bindings

nodes.summary: Let an LRU cache of capacity $c$ hold fewer than $c$ entries or already store a binding for the key $k$, and let $v$ be a value. Then a key-value pair $p$ is stored in the cache after putting the binding $(k, v)$ if and only if $p = (k, v)$, or $p$ was stored before and the key of $p$ differs from $k$.
nodes.title: Insertion without eviction

nodes.summary: For every LRU cache, key $k$ and value $v$, every key-value pair $p$ stored in the cache after putting the binding $(k, v)$ either equals $(k, v)$, or was stored before and has a key different from $k$.
nodes.title: Entries after insertion

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be an LRU cache of positive capacity, $k$ a key and $v$ a value. After the binding $(k, v)$ is put into $C$, the first entry of the resulting cache, its most recently used entry, is $(k, v)$.
nodes.title: With positive capacity, the inserted binding becomes the most recent entry

nodes.summary: For every LRU cache $C$, key $k$ and value $v$, the keys of the cache obtained by putting the binding $(k, v)$ into $C$ are pairwise distinct.
nodes.title: Insertion keeps the keys of an LRU cache distinct

nodes.summary: For every LRU cache $C$ of capacity $c$, key $k$ and value $v$, the cache obtained by putting the binding $(k, v)$ into $C$ has size at most $c$.
nodes.title: Insertion respects the capacity of an LRU cache

nodes.summary: Putting the binding $(k, v)$ into an LRU cache of capacity $c$ removes any entry with key $k$, places $(k, v)$ at the front as the most recently used entry, and then keeps only the first $c$ entries, so the least recently used entries beyond the capacity are evicted.
nodes.title: Insertion into an LRU cache

nodes.summary: Every LRU cache of capacity $c$ has size at most $c$.
nodes.title: An LRU cache never exceeds its capacity

nodes.summary: The size of an LRU cache is the number of entries it stores.
nodes.title: Size of an LRU cache

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.

breadcrumbs.label: Lists, stacks, queues and dynamic arrays
